intro_text: As they trudge through the snow, p_l spots a wolf pack round a kill in the distant valley below and calls app1 over.
decline_text: Thinking better of it, the cats try to hunt instead.

success_outcomes.text: It's a good opportunity to observe the dangerous predators from afar. app1 is surprised to watch them play, taking turns chasing and running from each other in a way that reminds them of the games they play with the other apprentices.

success_outcomes.text: The wolves seem sleepy and full of what used to be an adult elk, massive and spread out in bits across the valley. A coyote approaches and steals a bite. When the wolves notice and run the scavenger down, wagging their tails as they tear it apart, p_l and app1 watch silently, a grim reminder of what wolf packs are capable of.

success_outcomes.text: s_c wants to point out not the wolves, but the ravens around them. Wolves mostly tolerate ravens at their kills because it helps them find prey. Long ago, that bargain was offered to the cats of the world, but they foolishly betrayed the ravens and took the birds for food instead, and since then only the dogs have benefited from allies in the sky.

log.cats_from: from_cat taught to_cat about the history between ravens and wolves.
to_cat taught from_cat about the history between ravens and wolves.

success_outcomes.text: s_c shows app1 that, even from this distance, they can judge how the wolves killed their prey, nipping it to exhaustion and then wrestling it down. It's not c_n's usual way, but it's important to remember that whatever works, works. Something to keep in mind for app1 if {PRONOUN/app1/subject}{VERB/app1/'re/'s} ever part of a hunting patrol targeting large prey.

intro_text: p_l gathers some of {PRONOUN/p_l/poss} Clanmates, huddled together for warmth, and offers a tale to take everyone's mind off of the storm raging outside camp.
decline_text: The wind, howling and vast, drowns p_l out. There'll be no stories today.

success_outcomes.text: Once, long ago, cats roamed without a Clan, fending for themselves. Leaf-bare picked off the elderly, weak, and unlucky one by one, eating away at them. But one cat opened the warmth of their heart to shelter others in their nest, pelts sharing heat, many paws making light work. They became the first leader, and those cats, the first Clan.

log.cats_from: from_cat enjoyed to_cat's story about the creation of the first Clan.

fail_outcomes.text: p_l tries, but the wind keeps creeping through the outer walls of the den, and the story is cut short as the cats work to repair it. r_c starts shivering halfway through the repair job.

history_text.death: m_c died after getting too cold while repairing some dens.

intro_text: Many seasons ago, p_l begins, there was born a powerful, StarClan-gifted apprentice, one coveted by the Clans around them. Pulled in many directions, they could not keep the peace, as all demanded their time and skill.
decline_text: r_c doesn't have time to listen to p_l's story - {PRONOUN/r_c/subject} {VERB/r_c/apologize/apologizes}, but {PRONOUN/r_c/subject} rather {VERB/r_c/feel/feels} like that long dead overworked apprentice {PRONOUN/r_c/self}, right now!

success_outcomes.text: After moons of having their Clan attacked and targeted, the apprentice raged, calling on their hidden power. They summoned a powerful snowstorm and created leaf-bare in their anger before fleeing the Clans, never to return and never to walk the stars, their life and talents wasted by cruel petty fighting.

log.cats_from: from_cat enjoyed to_cat's story about the creation of leaf-bare.

fail_outcomes.text: Rudely, r_c leaves in the middle of p_l's tale, stealing the momentum from it. p_l trails off, embarrassed.

log.cats_from: p_l told a boring story about some special apprentice, and r_c wandered off in the middle.
log.cats_to: r_c wandered off at the most exciting part of p_l's tale of leaf-bare's creation.

intro_text: It's an old, important lesson. The apprentices are brought out to a valley, one side, steep, one shallow. The patrol settles on the shallow side, and the young cats are asked to study the clumped snow on the sharp wall across from them. Today, they will learn of avalanches.
decline_text: ...Or they would, if the valley wasn't so misted over it's barely possible to see the other side.

success_outcomes.text: The Mountain's Roar is not rage of blood and sinew, no anger of tooth or claw. It's unfeeling, unthinking, and uncaring, the deep rumble of the snowcaps themselves falling to their doom, p_l tells them. If they ever, ever feel their whiskers tremble with the noise, the only solution is to run - not down, but to the side, away from where the snow will flow. Do they understand?

success_outcomes.text: Somberly, p_l lists the cats {PRONOUN/p_l/subject} {VERB/p_l/know/knows} who died to an avalanche, who thought they were faster, who didn't heed the signs. Most of these cats were dead long before p_l was born, {PRONOUN/p_l/poss} knowledge of history going back generations, but this is what history is for. To learn from it.

success_outcomes.text: There are tricks to it, p_l explains. Avalanches fall like sudden floods of water or mud, but with unimaginable force. Survival is a matter of luck if they get caught. So don't get caught - run to the side of the slope, out of the path of the flow, horizontal. Climb, climb anything. The tree will get swept away, but they might float.
